name: Part naming evidence
description: Evidence about how proficient the student is at naming the plant part a diagram calls out.
claimStatement: The student's plant-part naming proficiency is high enough to select the name of the called-out part.
authoringNotes: 2PL updates the continuous naming proficiency. The binary Names the part attribute stays on the Q-matrix for the diagnostic model. Those two variables correlate. They are not the same variable.

warrants.reasoningStatement: Selecting the name of the called-out part is evidence about naming proficiency. A student higher on that trait is more likely to select the name.
warrants.performanceCondition: A flowering-plant diagram with one part called out, and four part names.
warrants.limitationClause: Does not show that the student can state the part's function.
warrants.backing: Plant-part naming research and the Grade 10 diagram curriculum.

observables.statement: The learner selects the name of the called-out plant part.

evidenceRule.activationCondition: The selected option is the name of the called-out part.
evidenceRule.justification: A correct selection is direct evidence of naming proficiency.

evidenceRules.activationCondition: The selected option is the name of the called-out part.
evidenceRules.justification: A correct selection is direct evidence of naming proficiency.

evaluationProcedures.description: The selected option is scored against the name of the called-out part.

decisionRule.justification: Pilot cut at 0 on the -3 to 3 scale. Calibration of the 2PL naming items replaces this threshold.

fairnessNotes: Diagrams use a standard flowering plant and everyday English part names. A student who has not seen this diagram style may miss the label rather than the part.

difReviewChecklist.prompt: Do the part names stay in everyday English?
Does the diagram show one familiar flowering plant?
Has a formal DIF study been run on these items?

calibrationPlan.method: Pilot the three naming items, then calibrate 2PL.

name: Part function evidence
description: Diagnostic evidence that the student can state what a named plant part does.
claimStatement: The student can state the function of a named plant part.

warrants.reasoningStatement: Choosing the job of a named part requires linking that structure to the work it does, and telling that job apart from where the part sits.
warrants.performanceCondition: The part is named in the stem. The options are functions, or a mix of functions and locations.
warrants.limitationClause: Does not show that the student can find the part on an unlabelled diagram.
warrants.backing: Structure-function studies of school biology and the named-part curriculum.

observables.statement: The learner selects the function of the named plant part.

evidenceRule.activationCondition: The selected option is the function of the named part.
evidenceRule.justification: A correct function is direct evidence of the function attribute.

observables.statement: The learner selects the sentence that states the part's function, rather than where the part is or what it looks like.

evidenceRule.activationCondition: The selected sentence states the function, not a location or a look.
evidenceRule.justification: Telling a function apart from a location is evidence of the function attribute.

evidenceRules.activationCondition: The selected option is the function of the named part.
evidenceRules.justification: A correct function is direct evidence of the function attribute.

evidenceRules.activationCondition: The selected sentence states the function, not a location or a look.
evidenceRules.justification: Telling a function apart from a location is evidence of the function attribute.

evaluationProcedures.description: A rater scores the chosen job of the named part with the plant function rubric.
A rater scores whether the chosen sentence states the function rather than a location.

decisionRule.justification: Mastery is a posterior at or above 0.75 on the function attribute until calibration replaces this pilot cut.

fairnessNotes: The stem names the part, so the item does not also test finding it on a diagram. Function words such as makes food and takes up water are everyday English.

difReviewChecklist.prompt: Does the stem name the part, so location is not a second hurdle?
Are the function phrases everyday English rather than technical terms?
Has a formal DIF study been run on these items?

calibrationPlan.method: Pilot the function items, then calibrate DINA on the plant Q-matrix.

name: Fraction evidence
description: Evidence that the student recognises equivalent fractions.
claimStatement: The student can identify a fraction equivalent to a given fraction, including its lowest-terms name.

warrants.reasoningStatement: Selecting 1/2 as equivalent to 2/4, or 2/3 as the lowest terms of 4/6, requires seeing that both names are the same amount.
warrants.performanceCondition: A stem fraction and four options. One option is equivalent, or is the lowest-terms name.
warrants.limitationClause: Does not show fluency with fraction arithmetic.
warrants.backing: Rational-number equivalence research and the Grade 10 fraction curriculum.

observables.statement: The learner selects the fraction equivalent to the stem fraction.

evidenceRule.activationCondition: The selected option is equivalent to the stem.
evidenceRule.justification: A correct selection is direct evidence of equivalence.

observables.statement: The learner selects the lowest-terms fraction that names the same amount as the stem.

evidenceRule.activationCondition: The selected option is the stem written in lowest terms.
evidenceRule.justification: Lowest terms is the same amount under the simplest name, so it supports equivalence.

evidenceRules.activationCondition: The selected option is equivalent to the stem.
evidenceRules.justification: A correct selection is direct evidence of equivalence.

evidenceRules.activationCondition: The selected option is the stem written in lowest terms.
evidenceRules.justification: Lowest terms is the same amount under the simplest name, so it supports equivalence.

evaluationProcedures.description: A rater scores whether the chosen fraction names the same amount as the stem.
A rater scores whether the chosen fraction is the stem written in lowest terms.

decisionRule.justification: Mastery is a posterior at or above 0.75 on the binary attribute. Calibration of the 1PL items replaces this pilot cut.

fairnessNotes: Stems use halves, thirds, and sixths with denominators at most 8. The wording is short. A student who has used fraction bars can still read the pair 2/4 and 1/2.

difReviewChecklist.prompt: Are the denominators small enough for Grade 6?
Does the stem avoid extra reading load beyond the fraction?
Has a formal DIF study been run on these items?

calibrationPlan.method: Pilot the equivalence items, then calibrate 1PL.
